long_biography.plain_text:
Murat Vargı spent years trying to persuade established Turkish business groups that mobile telephony could become a mass market. Drawing on export experience at Koç Holding and his own trading companies, he developed the project, brought Ericsson into the effort and found the financial partners needed to launch Turkcell. The service began operating when Turkey's telecommunications market was still dominated by the state, and Vargı remained closely involved as the company scaled and listed internationally.

Vargı used MV Holding to carry the entrepreneurial model into other sectors. The group became a founding partner of mobile-device distributor KVK, later established a majority-owned wind-power business and developed hotels, student accommodation, technology ventures and a broad financial-investment portfolio. He now serves as MV Holding's honorary president. Outside business, he chairs Çöpüne Sahip Çık, a foundation that promotes waste reduction and environmental awareness, and sits on education-foundation boards.
